title: Kestrel Insurance — integration & technical gaps
content:
Context:
Customer: Kestrel Insurance (mid-size regional insurer). Exploring a 3-month pilot to automate first-touch claims triage and policy lookup augmentation. Primary contact: Marco (CTO), technical lead: Priya (platform), business lead: Hannah (ops).

Call summary (2026-02-26):
- Demo: quick walkthrough of hosted API + private deployment options. They liked streaming for agent-assist.
- Key asks: private network option (VPC peering), PII redaction at inference time, 99ms median latency target for short prompts (under 128 tokens) for agent UI, and audit log retention for 13 months.
- Data flows: claims PDF -> OCR pipeline (3rd party) -> internal policy DB (on-prem Postgres) -> call to Redwood model for summary + triage label. They prefer no raw PII leaving their network.

Technical notes / gotchas:
- Their Postgres sits in a legacy datacenter behind an L4-only LB; no easy way to run push-based connectors from our hosted plane. Likely requires Private (VPC) or on-prem connector.
- They insist on customer-managed KMS for keys (HSM). Need to confirm Redwood Private supports external KMS integration in current packaging.
- Latency target 99ms median is aggressive. Sample prompt sizes small but concurrency will be bursty during shift start. Need to evaluate batching/caching tradeoffs.
- OCR output has inconsistent structured fields (claimant name, DOB) — will need schema mapping to reliably redact PII before sending.
- Compliance: regulator requires 13 months of immutable audit logs; our current hosted retention defaults are 90 days unless add-on purchased. Also need tamper-evidence requirements clarified.
- Model choice: they asked about smaller LLMs for cost control + deterministic outputs. We should propose a quantized 7B variant with retrieval augmentation for factuality. Verify we have compatibility with their tokens-per-call expectations.

Open questions (for internal follow-up):
- Can Redwood Private be provisioned into their VPC with customer KMS (HSM) and meet 13-month immutable audit storage? (owner: Marco? No, internal owner: Liam)
- What are SLA guarantees for cross-region failover if they request secondary region? (owner: SRE team — tag JIRA-INFRA-578)
- Is there an off-the-shelf PII redaction preprocessor we can ship, or do they need to run that inside their network? (owner: Priya)
- What will typical QPS look like during peak (they promised to share traffic histogram)? Without that, can't size Dedicated pool. (owner: Asha — follow up w/ Hannah)

Immediate next steps (concrete):
1) Asha: Send summary + required artifacts list to Marco & Priya by 2026-02-27. Ask for: sample redacted/unredacted OCR outputs, expected QPS per hour, IP ranges for peering.
2) Liam: Kick off internal pre-check on Private KMS support and HSM compliance (create JIRA-SE-1421) — due 2026-03-05.
3) Priya: Share one example policy lookup flow (SQL schema, typical latency) and confirm whether DB can accept an outbound push connector or only inbound queries via LB. Due 2026-03-03.
4) Marco/Priya: Confirm retention and immutability requirements (legal/regulator doc) and share sample language. Due 2026-03-06.
5) Engineering (Marco Li): Quick benchmarking task — run a micro-benchmark on the quantized 7B variant for 64-token prompts to estimate median latency at 1, 5, 10 QPS. Create GH issue and link. Due 2026-03-07.

Notes to self (informal):
- Likely path: Redwood Private in their VPC + customer KMS + local PII redaction before hitting inference. Hosted not acceptable for now.
- Watch for procurement/legal: 13-month audit retention + HSM will push this into enterprise legal review. Need to flag to account team early.
- Consider offering a narrow-scope managed integration package: set up VPC peering, KMS config, and a redaction Lambda skeleton they can run. Price it as a 3-month onboarding.

Risks / blockers:
- If their datacenter network cannot be peered (security forbids), on-prem install will be much heavier and likely extend pilot timeline 6+ weeks.
- OCR/PII mapping is messy — accuracy here determines whether model sees PII at all.

Meeting artifacts to attach once received:
- sample_claims_ocr.zip (they will send)
- policy_lookup_schema.pdf
- regulator-data-retention.pdf
- network-allowlist.csv

Slack threads / refs:
- internal: https://slack.redwood.com/archives/SE-team/p02kestrel (contains the meeting recording clip)
- sales thread: https://slack.redwood.com/archives/GTMSALES/p03kestrel-deal

Thoughts for solutioning (very rough):
- Option A: Private deployment (single AZ) with VPC peering + HSM KMS, pre-ingest PII redaction in customer network, store 13-month logs in their S3 with immutable flags, Redwood runs inference in their VPC.
- Option B: On-prem package (if peering impossible) — heavier but meets data sovereignty. Need infra checklist for ops.
- Cost levers: recommend quantized model + strict max tokens + per-request streaming disabled unless agent needs it.

Last note: keep this doc lean — once we have artifacts attach and convert to a Confluence onboarding playbook.

-- Asha
